classification.difficultyReason: Translate half an annulus into a fraction of the outer circle, cancel the area factors, then use numerator splitting and positivity to justify a strict bound.

content.prompt: The inner radius is $r>0$ and the outer radius is $kr$, where $k>1$. Half the ring is shaded. Find the shaded fraction of the outer circle. Can it ever equal one half? Explain by splitting the numerator.

spec.description: Concentric circles with half the ring shaded. Schematic radii r and kr; k>1.
spec.mathematics: Inner radius r>0, outer radius kr, k>1. Shaded area is half the annulus.

answer.short: $\dfrac{k^2-1}{2k^2}=\dfrac12-\dfrac{1}{2k^2}<\dfrac12$. Since $k>1$, the subtracted term is positive, so it never equals one half.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}}&=\pi(kr)^2=\pi k^2r^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac12(\pi k^2r^2-\pi r^2)\\f&=\frac{\frac12\pi r^2(k^2-1)}{\pi k^2r^2}\\f&=\frac{k^2-1}{2k^2}\\f&=\frac{k^2}{2k^2}-\frac1{2k^2}\\f&=\frac12-\frac1{2k^2}\end{align*}$$
For every $k>1$, $\frac1{2k^2}>0$, so the shaded fraction is always less than one half and can never equal it.
